A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FICTION work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. Text comparison and visual inspection support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original interaction-location and pose-prediction experiments on Ego-Exo4D, including baseline comparisons in Table 1 and ablations in Tables 2–5.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds quantitative validation of extracted poses in Appendix B and qualitative baseline comparisons in Figure 5.

M1.justification: The multimodal transformer, voxel location decoder, conditional pose model, losses, and inference procedures remain unchanged. Selecting the view with maximum joint visibility and using N=16 were already specified in v1; v2 adds justification for these choices.

E1.justification: Both versions cover interaction-location and pose forecasting in Ego-Exo4D cooking, bike repair, and health scenarios. The added pose-quality check uses a manually annotated subset within the existing dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains HierVL, OCT, OccFormer, and VoxFormer for location prediction, and 4D-Humans, T2M-GPT, T2M-GPT-FT, and Video-to-pose for pose prediction. Appendix C retains their adaptations. Figure 5 illustrates existing baseline families without introducing a new named comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix B adds an evaluation against manually annotated 3D poses, comparing maximum-joint-visibility and maximum-hand-visibility view selection using MPJPE. The subset size is unspecified. Existing splits, training settings, prediction horizons, metrics, and best-of-five pose evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a pose-extraction quality analysis comparing two view-selection criteria and qualitative baseline comparisons for cooking and bike repair in Figure 5. The existing modality ablations and observation-time, prediction-horizon, learning-rate, and model-size analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added pose-quality results are point estimates without uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Appendix B newly reports 82 mm MPJPE for maximum joint visibility versus 115 mm for maximum hand visibility. Figure 5 adds qualitative comparison results. All numerical entries in Table 1 and Tables 2–5 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The task definitions, Equations 1–2, and training-loss mathematics are unchanged. The added N^3 parameter-scaling remark explains the existing voxel decoder; no new derivation, proof, or formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same central contributions: long-horizon 4D interaction prediction, explicit scene-conditioned location and pose forecasting, and the curated Ego-Exo4D benchmark. The abstract and introduction retain the claim of more than 30% relative gains.

C2.justification: Section 3.4 adds a resolution-versus-memory rationale for N=16 and explains parameter scaling with voxel resolution. Appendix B adds support for prioritizing overall joint visibility. The single-actor, static-point-cloud, and extraction-error limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds technical explanation of voxel-resolution feasibility and parameter scaling. Section 3.3 changes the data-release statement from 'will share' to 'are sharing', although Appendix A still promises future data/code release, leaving availability unclear. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, and access link are retained.

R1.justification: The reference list is unchanged, as is the positioning against 2D anticipation, short-horizon pose forecasting, and single-object interaction work. Local wording edits and repeated citations do not substantively change the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: V2 makes local grammar and wording edits, expands the institutional affiliation, and adds short explanatory and analytical passages. The main section order and Appendix A–E structure remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figure 5 and reflows the appendix, moving Table 5 and the limitations section onto the final page. Several image insets in Figures 1 and 4 are downsampled; for example, Figure 4 observation frames decrease from 798×800 to 130×130 pixels while retaining the same examples.

improvement.justification: The added pose-quality validation provides evidence for an existing preprocessing choice, while Figure 5 and the voxel-resolution explanation improve inspectability and technical clarity. These are limited gains: the main results are unchanged, the validation subset size and uncertainty are unspecified, and Figure 5 identifies only baseline families. Lower-resolution insets in existing figures modestly offset the benefits.
